To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of litter fungi fruiting bodies was not random in the landscape in a tropical ever-green forest in Central Amazon, that rainfall influenced fungal diversity and that edaphic factors also influenced the distribution of fungi.

Fungi are important in tropical ecosystems and there is a lack of information on how they are distributed in the landscape; we tested if the fruiting bodies of fungi were randomly distributed in a tropical ever green forest in Central Amazon; we used regression analyses to evaluate the influence on fungal richness and composition of rainfall, soil, and topography; and we showed that fungal species are not randomly distributed and that it is viable, if the temporal, spatial, and temporal × spatial interactions are taken into account,

the distribution of litter fungi is not random in the landscape, that rainfall and edaphic factors influence litter fungal diversity in Central Amazonia and that it is viable for mesoscale evaluations to be carried out, if temporal and spatial variation are considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how fungal diversity is distributed in space.
how the species of fungi are distributed in the landscape and how this distribution can be related to environmental factors.
the spatial and temporal patterns of fungal fruiting body distribution in the landscape of a Central Amazonian evergreen forest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the distribution of fruit body of litter fungi in the landscape is influenced by rainfall, soil and altitude, and that it is feasible to conduct mesoscales studies of fungal diversity, provided that temporal and spatial variation, and their interaction, are taken into account.
the study shows the importance of considering rainfall and edaphic factors when evaluating fungal diversity, especially in the tropics, where rainfall is highly seasonal.

Fungi are important in the recycling of tropical ecosystems, however, there is little data about how fungal diversity is distributed in the landscape, which is necessary for planning their conservation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution of fruitbodies of litter fungi was influenced by short-term rainfall and soil clay content, and the influence of edaphic factors on fungi depended on the amount of rainfall.
we found a significant influence of rainfall and soil clay content on fungal morphospecies richness.

we have demonstrated that the distribution of fruit bodies of litter fungi is non-random in a tropical forest, and we have shown the influence of environmental factors on the distribution and composition of litter fungal species in a tropical forest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the species of leaf litter fungi are not distributed randomly in the landscape.
it is viable for us to plan the conservation of fungal diversity at mesoscales (25-1000 km2), if the temporal and the spatial variation and their interactions are considered.
the distribution of fruit bodies of litter fungi in the Central Amazonian forest is not random.
